subject: English Language
text: Neither the manager nor the assistants ____ ready to leave.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'assistants' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: We ____ to meet the client at 9 am tomorrow.
explanation: Present continuous (are meeting) expresses a planned arrangement with a fixed time more naturally than bare future.

subject: English Language
text: His explanation was so _____ that everyone understood immediately.
explanation: 'Lucid' means clear and easily understood; contrasts with 'ambiguous' and 'cryptic' which mean unclear.

subject: English Language
text: She told him to keep his ______ about the negotiation.
explanation: The idiom 'keep one's head' means to stay calm; 'keep his head' is the correct idiomatic choice here.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly capitalised sentence: 'the bishop of lagos addressed the congregation.'
options: The Bishop of Lagos addressed the congregation.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Titles that refer to a specific office as a proper noun (Bishop of Lagos) are capitalised; 'Lagos' is a proper noun too.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable is stressed in the word 'photograph'?
explanation: 'Photograph' has primary stress on the first syllable: 'PHO-to-graph'. This is a standard stress pattern.

subject: English Language
text: Which pair of words rhyme?
explanation: 'Fight' and 'right' rhyme because they share the same vowel and final consonant sound; others do not rhyme.

subject: English Language
text: Each of the students should submit ____ essay.
explanation: 'Each' is singular; grammatically correct traditional agreement uses 'his or her' to match singular antecedent.

subject: English Language
text: Combine into one sentence using 'enough': He is too young. He cannot vote.
options: He is not old enough to vote.
He is too young enough to vote.
He is enough too young to vote.
He is not too enough to vote.
explanation: Correct transformation: 'not old enough' expresses the same meaning; other options are ungrammatical or nonsensical.

subject: English Language
text: The committee will meet on Friday, ____ the venue is still undecided.
explanation: 'Although' (or 'though') properly links the two clauses expressing contrast after a comma; 'unless' and 'whereas' do not fit the contrast here.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence expresses a polite request?
options: Could you please pass the salt?
explanation: 'Could you please pass the salt?' is a polite interrogative request form; the imperative 'Pass the salt.' is less polite.

subject: English Language
text: Ada used a calendar app to set reminders for her bills; last month none of her payments were late. What does this most likely imply?
options: She did not have many bills.
She forgot to check her calendar.
The app helped her pay on time.
explanation: The sequence suggests causation: setting reminders led to timely payments. This most plausibly implies the app helped her pay on time.

subject: English Language
text: A bouquet of roses ____ on the table.
explanation: Subject 'a bouquet' is singular; use singular verb 'is'. Collective noun agreement requires verb to agree with the head noun.

subject: English Language
text: By the time she joined the meeting, they ____ lunch.
explanation: Past perfect 'had started' indicates the action (starting lunch) occurred before another past event (she joined). Use past perfect for the earlier past action.

subject: English Language
text: The scientist's theory was ____ by new evidence.
explanation: Context needs a verb meaning 'shown to be right' — 'vindicated'. 'Vindication' is a noun, 'vindictive' an adjective, 'veneration' means respect.

subject: English Language
text: He decided to bite the bullet and ____.
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' is an idiom meaning to accept or endure something difficult; only 'face the difficult task' matches that sense.

subject: English Language
text: the foreign minister of ghana visited accra last week.
options: The Foreign Minister of Ghana visited Accra last week.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Capitals required for sentence start, official title and proper nouns: 'The', 'Foreign Minister', 'Ghana', and city 'Accra'. Title words are capitalised in this use.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable is stressed in the word 'photography'?
explanation: 'Photography' is pronounced /fəˈtɒgrəfi/ with primary stress on the second syllable. Stress placement distinguishes related words (photography vs photograph).

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the long vowel sound /i:/?
explanation: 'Seat' contains the long vowel /i:/. 'Sit' has /ɪ/, 'set' has /ɛ/, 'sat' has /æ/. Long vs short vowel contrast is phonemic.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is an offer?
options: Would you mind opening the window?
explanation: 'Shall I carry your bag?' offers to do something for someone. The others are requests or commands, not offers.

subject: English Language
text: Change to passive: 'They will announce the results tomorrow.'
options: The results will be announced tomorrow.
Tomorrow the results were announced by them.
The results are announced tomorrow by them.
Announced tomorrow will be the results.
explanation: Passive of future simple uses 'will be' + past participle: 'The results will be announced tomorrow.' Other options show wrong tense or ungrammatical order.

subject: English Language
text: If she ____ earlier, she would not have missed the train.
explanation: Third conditional requires past perfect in the if-clause: 'If she had left earlier...' to express an unreal past condition and its past consequence.

subject: English Language
text: Mark's tone was curt during the interview.
explanation: 'Curt' describes speech that is brief and abrupt, often perceived as rude or unfriendly; it does not mean polite, long, or hesitant.

subject: English Language
text: Excuse me Maria can you help me?
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
Excuse me, Maria, can you help me?
explanation: When directly addressing someone (vocative), commas set off the name: 'Excuse me, Maria, can you help me?' Commas before and after the name are required here.

subject: English Language
text: Ten naira ____ enough to buy the book.
explanation: Monetary amounts (sums of money) are treated as singular nouns, so use 'is' for agreement.

subject: English Language
text: By noon tomorrow, I ____ the report.
explanation: The future perfect ('will have finished') shows an action completed before a specified future time.

subject: English Language
text: He sings ____ than his brother.
explanation: Comparing manner requires an adverb; the comparative adverb form is 'more beautifully'.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly capitalised sentence: 'the minister of education will visit kano.'
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
The Minister of Education will visit Kano.
explanation: Official titles and proper nouns are capitalised: 'Minister of Education' and place names like 'Kano'.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable is stressed in the word 'banana'?
explanation: The primary stress in 'banana' falls on the second syllable: ba-NA-na, so the 2nd syllable is stressed.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the vowel sound /ɔː/ as in 'law'?
explanation: The vowel /ɔː/ (as in 'law') appears in 'caught'; 'cat', 'coat', and 'cut' have different vowel phonemes.

subject: English Language
text: Which completes the idiom: 'After the scandal, the politician had to eat ___.'
explanation: The idiom is 'eat humble pie', meaning to accept humiliation or admit error; 'humble pie' is the fixed phrase.

subject: English Language
text: Combine using 'although': 'She failed the exam. She had studied hard.'
options: She failed the exam although had studied hard.
Although she studied hard she had failed the exam.
She had studied hard although she failed the exam.
Although she had studied hard, she failed the exam.
explanation: Correct subordinate clause order: 'Although she had studied hard, she failed the exam.' preserves tense and contrast.

subject: English Language
text: If you ___ earlier, you would have caught the bus.
explanation: This is a third conditional: use past perfect in the 'if' clause ('had left') with 'would have' in the result clause.

subject: English Language
text: The meeting was perfunctory. Which best interprets 'perfunctory'?
explanation: 'Perfunctory' describes something done superficially or with minimal effort; it implies brief, routine performance.

subject: English Language
text: Which is an indirect question?
options: Could you tell me where she went?
explanation: An indirect question is politely phrased and retains statement word order: 'Could you tell me where she went?' is indirect.

subject: English Language
text: _____ apples are in the basket?
explanation: 'Apples' is countable; use 'How many' for questions about quantity with countable nouns.

subject: English Language
text: Each of the participants ____ a badge.
explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb. Use 'has' not 'have' or plural forms; rule of concord: each + singular verb.

subject: English Language
text: By the end of the month she ____ her manuscript.
explanation: Future perfect ('will have submitted') expresses completion before a future time; 'will submit' does not show completion by that time.

subject: English Language
text: Change to passive: 'A technician will repair the generator tomorrow.'
options: A technician will be repaired by the generator tomorrow.
Tomorrow the generator will repair a technician.
The generator will be repaired by a technician tomorrow.
The generator will have been repaired by a technician yesterday.
explanation: Passive form places object first with correct auxiliary: 'will be' + past participle; option 1 correctly keeps tense and agent.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: Sade said, "I'll join you at noon."
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
Sade said, "I'll join you at noon."
explanation: Standard dialogue tag uses comma then quoted sentence with initial capital; 'noon' is a common noun not capitalised; option 2 follows these conventions.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable is stressed in the word 'photographer'?
explanation: 'Photographer' has primary stress on the second syllable (pho-TOG-ra-pher); stress shifts from 'photograph' to the second syllable in 'photographer'.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the vowel sound /ʊ/ as in 'put'?
explanation: The vowel in 'book' is /ʊ/ (as in 'put'); 'boot' is /uː/, 'bait' is /eɪ/, 'but' is /ʌ/—different vowel qualities.

subject: English Language
text: In 'Resilient local businesses recovered quickly after the flood,' 'resilient' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Resilient' means able to withstand or recover quickly from difficulties; it does not mean wealthy, new, or merely stubborn.

subject: English Language
text: In 'The manager warned against cutting corners on safety,' 'cutting corners' means:
explanation: 'Cutting corners' idiomatically means doing less than is needed to save time or cost, producing careless or incomplete work, not simply saving money correctly.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence expresses advice?
options: You should see a doctor about that cough.
Would you mind bringing the file?
explanation: 'You should...' is a typical structure for advice; other options are a request, a statement of fact, and an expression of gratitude respectively.

subject: English Language
text: After the audit, the team found minor discrepancies but no evidence of fraud. The most reasonable conclusion is:
options: The company is innocent of any dishonesty.
The discrepancies are likely unintentional and do not indicate fraud.
The auditors failed to detect serious problems.
Fraud will certainly be discovered later.
explanation: Finding minor discrepancies with no evidence of fraud supports the inference that errors are likely unintentional; it stops short of proving absolute innocence or predicting future fraud.

subject: English Language
text: Change to reported speech: "Don't forget to lock the door," she said to Mark.
options: She said Mark not to forget to lock the door.
She reminded Mark not forgetting the door to lock.
She told Mark not to forget to lock the door.
She told Mark forgot to lock the door.
explanation: Direct command with a negative becomes 'told Mark not to...' or 'reminded Mark to...'; option 1 correctly uses 'told' + negative infinitive structure for reported speech.

subject: English Language
text: She is the only one of the candidates who ____ the necessary experience.
explanation: 'The only one' is singular; the relative clause refers to that singular antecedent, so singular verb 'has' is required despite 'candidates' appearing after 'of'.

subject: English Language
text: Either the principal or the teachers ____ responsible for the schedule.
explanation: With 'either...or' the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Teachers' is plural, so use 'are'. This is the nearest-subject agreement rule.

subject: English Language
text: By 5 pm today I ____ the grant application.
explanation: Future perfect ('will have submitted') expresses completion before a specified future time (by 5 pm). Other forms do not show future completion.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'Her stoicism impressed the team,' stoicism most nearly means:
explanation: Stoicism refers to control of emotion and endurance under hardship; 'calm endurance' captures this meaning unlike the other choices.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the idiom: 'When push comes to ___'.
explanation: The established idiom is 'when push comes to shove', meaning when a situation becomes serious or urgent; 'shove' is the conventional word.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly capitalised sentence: 'senator chukwuma will address the assembly on Monday.'
options: Senator Chukwuma will address the assembly on Monday.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Capitals: titles before names (Senator), proper names (Chukwuma), and days (Monday). 'assembly' is common unless it is an official proper name, so lower-case is correct here.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable is stressed in the word 'instrumental'?
explanation: The primary stress in 'instrumental' is on the third syllable: in-stru-MEN-tal (phonetic pattern /ˌɪnstrəˈmentəl/), so the third option is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the vowel sound /ʌ/ as in 'cup'?
explanation: 'Come' is pronounced /kʌm/ with the /ʌ/ vowel (as in 'cup'). 'Coat' /oʊ/, 'car' /ɑː/ (or /a/), 'case' /eɪ/ are different vowel sounds.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is a polite request?
options: Bring the files to my office now.
I will send the revised draft by noon.
I suggest we delay the meeting.
Could you send the revised draft by noon?
explanation: 'Could you...' is a conventional polite request using a modal question form; the others are commands, statements, or suggestions, not polite requests.

subject: English Language
text: Change to passive: 'The board appointed Nneka chairperson yesterday.'
options: Nneka was appointed chairperson by the board yesterday.
Nneka appointed as chairperson by the board yesterday.
The board was appointed chairperson yesterday by Nneka.
Nneka had been appointed chairperson yesterday by the board.
explanation: Passive of past simple: object becomes subject ('Nneka'), verb becomes 'was appointed', and agent is 'by the board'. Option 1 follows standard passive formation and tense.

subject: English Language
text: If I ____ the report now, I will finish before lunch.
explanation: First conditional uses present simple in the 'if' clause + 'will' in the main clause. 'If I start... I will finish' follows this rule; other forms are incorrect.

subject: English Language
text: Amina left her umbrella at the bus stop; it rained heavily that afternoon. The most reasonable inference is that:
options: Amina avoided the rain by using a different umbrella.
The bus stop staff returned the umbrella immediately.
Amina likely got wet after losing her umbrella.
It did not rain where Amina was.
explanation: Given she left her umbrella and heavy rain occurred, the simplest inference is she likely got wet. The other choices require extra unsupported assumptions.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: Maria asked, 'When will the meeting start?'
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
Maria asked, 'When will the meeting start?'
explanation: Correct punctuation includes a comma before a direct quotation and capitalising the quoted sentence. The question mark belongs inside the quotation marks; option 1 follows these rules.
